Simulate outcomes from a fitted choice model

Source: R/methods.R
simulate.choicemodel.Rd

Draws nsim outcome vectors from the fitted model (holding the covariates fixed): the parametric bootstrap of the model. For every family but the random-intercept one the draw of a case is from its fitted probabilities of the observed alternatives (the GHK probabilities of a multinomial probit case are renormalized to one); for remnl() one intercept vector is drawn per unit and the unit's cases are then drawn given it, so the within-unit dependence of the model is reproduced. Frequency weights are left as they are: one draw per row, so for a weighted fit the draws are not the parametric bootstrap of the weighted data (a row of weight w would need w draws; boot_pvalue() expands the rows for that reason). For nominal outcomes there is no meaningful residual ordering, so these draws serve test calibration and predictive checks rather than DHARMa-style quantile residuals.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'choicemodel'
simulate(object, nsim = 1, seed = NULL, ..., ties = c("untied", "observed"))

Arguments

object

A "choicemodel" fit.

nsim

Number of simulated outcome vectors.

seed

Optional seed (as in stats::simulate(); the caller's random-number stream is restored afterwards).

...

Unused.

ties

For a rologit() fit: "untied" (default), every case ranking as many positions as it ranked in the data, without ties; or "observed", each case's observed pattern of rank groups (the same group sizes in the same order, a tie staying a tie at its positions), as boot_lr_test() draws rankings.

Value

A data frame with nsim factor columns (sim_1, ...), one row per estimation case. For a rologit() fit, a list of nsim integer matrices (cases by alternatives) of simulated ranks (0 for the unranked and unavailable alternatives).
